echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Duplication gate (production JS duplicated lines <= 1%, ratcheted)
        # Ratchet, not an absolute bar: a pinned set of production JS files
        # already exceeds 1% duplicated lines — pre-existing debt owned by the
        # gh-1244…gh-1250 dedup tickets (see duplication-baseline.json for the
        # current pinned set) — so the measurement's exit 2 is expected for
        # now. The baseline pins each over-threshold file with its measured
        # percentage and absolute duplicated-line count; the gate FAILS only
        # on a NEW over-threshold file or a pinned file that gained ABSOLUTE
        # duplicated lines (ci/duplicationRatchet.js) — a percentage shift
        # caused by file shrinkage passes and is logged as informational —
        # keeping the absolute 1% bar as the end state once the debt lands.
        # A crashed measurement (tool exit other than 0/2) never passes.
        # js/unit-tests/** stays excluded; the badge step below reparses the
        # same measurement for the README endpoint.
        run: |
          set +e
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" duplicates --threshold 1 --exclude "js/unit-tests/**" js ci > "$RUNNER_TEMP/dup-gate.txt" 2>&1
          code=$?
          set -e
          node ci/duplicationRatchet.js "$RUNNER_TEMP/dup-gate.txt" duplication-baseline.json "$code"

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# ── Ensure Node/npm/npx are on PATH even in non-interactive shells ───────────
# Several providers below shell out to `npx @github/copilot@...`/`npx
# @anthropic-ai/claude-code` etc. when the CLI binary itself isn't globally
# installed. Node is typically managed by nvm, and nvm only auto-loads via
# ~/.bashrc — but ~/.bashrc's very first lines ("If not running
# interactively, don't do anything") make it a no-op for any NON-interactive
# shell, including `bash -lc "..."` (which is exactly how dmtools/Java spawns
# this script via ProcessBuilder, and how run-teammate-local.sh/CI invoke it
# too). Without this, every `npx ...` call fails outright with
# "npx: command not found" (exit 127) — but the surrounding Teammate job
# still reports success and its postJSAction still advances the ticket
# (labels + status change), producing a "completed" run that silently wrote
# NO content at all (see e.g. agents/js/assignForSolutionArchitecture.js).
# Guarded on `command -v npx` so this is a fast no-op once Node is already
# resolvable (global install, PATH already exporting nvm's bin dir, etc).
if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  if [ -s "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" ]; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    \. "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" --no-use
    nvm use default >/dev/null 2>&1 || nvm use node >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
fi

# Load shared helpers and provider implementations.
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/_common.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/claude.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/codemie.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/copilot.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/fa.sh"

# ── Agent docs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Regenerate docs/agents/generated/* whenever agent configs, JS actions,
# instructions, prompts, human docs, or the generator itself change.

DOC_GENERATOR="$REPO_ROOT/js/agentDocGenerator.js"
DOCS_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/docs/agents"

NEEDS_DOC_REGEN=false
for f in $STAGED_FILES; do
    case "$f" in
        *.json|js/*.js|js/common/*.js|instructions/*|prompts/*|docs/agents/*.md|js/agentDocGenerator.js)
            NEEDS_DOC_REGEN=true
            break
            ;;
    esac
done

if [ "$NEEDS_DOC_REGEN" = "true" ]; then
    echo "🔄 Regenerating agent docs..."
    node "$DOC_GENERATOR"
    if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
        echo "❌ Agent docs generation failed. Fix errors above and retry."
        exit 1
    fi
    UPDATED_DOCS=$(git diff --name-only "$DOCS_DIR" 2>/dev/null)
    UNTRACKED_DOCS=$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard "$DOCS_DIR" 2>/dev/null)
    if [ -n "$UPDATED_DOCS" ] || [ -n "$UNTRACKED_DOCS" ]; then
        git add "$DOCS_DIR"
        echo "✅ Agent docs regenerated and staged automatically."
    fi

# Call this immediately before invoking the CLI provider.
start_output_rescue_marker() {
  mktemp
}

# Defense-in-depth against agent working-directory drift.
#
# Coding-agent CLIs (Claude Code, Copilot CLI, etc.) typically run their Bash
# tool as ONE persistent shell across the whole session — a `cd` in one tool
# call carries over to every later call, including the final `Write` of
# outputs/response.md (or outputs/pr_review.json, outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md,
# etc). When an agent explores a dependency checkout (`cd dependencies/<repo>
# && ...`) to read source while producing its own output, and never `cd`s
# back to the job root before writing outputs/*, those files silently land
# under dependencies/<repo>/outputs/... instead of ./outputs/. The agent's own
# tool result still reports success ("File created successfully at:
# outputs/response.md") because that path really was created — just relative
# to the wrong cwd. Left undetected, dmtools then reports "did not produce
# output file", skips the Jira field update, and posts a giant raw-log
# fallback comment that itself is too long to post — a fully silent failure
# with no usable content anywhere.
#
# This rescues ANY output file misplaced this way — not just response.md —
# by searching for other outputs/ directories created/modified since
# start_output_rescue_marker() was called, and copying their newer files up
# into the job's own ./outputs/. It never overwrites a file that's already
# correctly present at the real ./outputs/ path (that one is trusted as
# authoritative).
#
# Usage:
#   local marker; marker="$(start_output_rescue_marker)"
#   run_claude_code || exit_code=$?
#   rescue_misplaced_outputs "$marker"
#   rm -f "$marker"
rescue_misplaced_outputs() {
  local start_marker="$1"
  local root_outputs="./outputs"
  local rescued=0

  if [ -z "$start_marker" ] || [ ! -e "$start_marker" ]; then
    return 0
  fi

  local candidate_dir
  while IFS= read -r -d '' candidate_dir; do
    local misplaced_file
    while IFS= read -r -d '' misplaced_file; do
      local rel_path="${misplaced_file#"${candidate_dir}"/}"
      local dest="${root_outputs}/${rel_path}"
      if [ -e "$dest" ]; then
        echo "⚠️  Found misplaced output '${misplaced_file}' but '${dest}' already exists at the job root — leaving both, not overwriting"
        continue
      fi
      mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest")" 2>/dev/null || {
        echo "⚠️  Could not create directory for rescued output '${dest}' — skipping this file (original left untouched at '${misplaced_file}')"
        continue
      }
      if cp -p "$misplaced_file" "$dest" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "⚠️  Rescued misplaced output: '${misplaced_file}' -> '${dest}' (agent's shell working directory likely drifted into '${candidate_dir%/outputs}' before writing — check its final cd/pwd discipline)"
        rescued=$((rescued + 1))
      fi
    done < <(find "$candidate_dir" -type f -newer "$start_marker" -print0 2>/dev/null)
  done < <(find . -maxdepth 6 -type d -name outputs \
              -not -path "./outputs" \
              -not -path "*/.git/*" \
              -not -path "*/node_modules/*" \
              -not -path "*/vendor/*" \
              -print0 2>/dev/null)

  if [ "$rescued" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "⚠️  Rescued ${rescued} misplaced output file(s) into ${root_outputs}/ — see warnings above."

`postDevelopTicketDynamicRepo.js` delegates to `developAndPR.action(params)` — full shared flow including both surfaces. ✅

Final matrix confirmed. Now let me also double-check one remaining wrinkle in the test file: the loader `loadForConcernsSeam` mocks `'./common/outputFiles.js'` with `concernsSeamOutputFilesStub(opts)` where `readOutputFile` doubles as the response.md reader — but in production `readResponseMd` calls `outputFiles.readOutputFile('response.md', {ticketKey, workingDir})`. The stub ignores args — fine for characterization.

One more check — `writeConcernsIntoResponseMd(ctx, ...)` takes `ctx` and uses only `ctx.ticketKey`. In `mirrorConcernsIntoResponseBody(ctx, responseContent)` — passes ctx. Fine. Unused param? No, used.

Also `mirrorConcernsIntoResponseBody` wraps `writeConcernsIntoResponseMd` in try/catch AND `writeConcernsIntoResponseMd` itself has no try — the catch in mirror covers file_write failures ("a failing response.md write keeps the mirror best-effort" test). But note: if `file_write` fails AFTER... no partial-write concern in dmtools (atomic enough). Fine.

Now — severity calibration for the two main findings:

**Finding 1: bug_fix_batch_development leg — instructed but not wired.**
- Evidence (all read this run):
 - `bug_fix_batch_development.json` cliPrompts includes `./agents/instructions/bug_development/general_guidelines.md` but not `./agents/instructions/common/completion_post_check.md`
 - `instructions/bug_development/general_guidelines.md` hunks (diff): new POSTCHECK node + "Before finishing, run the COMPLETION POST-CHECK" line
 - `snapshots/bug_fix_batch_development.md` hunks: the batch prompt bundle now contains the POSTCHECK flow + the reference line (author regenerated it)
 - `js/developBugFixBatchAndCreatePR.js`: grep shows no concerns/appendConcerns/mirror wiring; it builds its own PR body and comments.
- Result: batch agents write `outputs/concerns.md` nobody reads; gaps never surfaced; also the check definition file isn't in the bundle (agent must self-locate it, inconsistent with the bundling convention the PR itself follows for the other two configs).
- Severity: BLOCKING (broken behavior introduced by the diff on a shipped leg). The PR description only claims bug_development + story_development — this is also a silent scope leak.

**Finding 2: response.md clobber hazard on transient re-read failure.**
- `writeConcernsIntoResponseMd` (js/developTicketAndCreatePR.js:614-625): `readResponseMd(...) || ''` → blank base → `file_write({path:'outputs/response.md', content: concerns-only})` overwrites the leg deliverable. Pinned by the test "response.md unreadable while concerns exist → section still appended to an empty base".
- Severity: IMPORTANT (low-probability transient read failure; permanent loss of the PR body source; cheap guard: skip the write when the base read comes back null, or write back to the detailed-read hit path).

**Finding 3 (SUGESTION): `readConcernsMd` docstring claims "same candidate expansion as every other output file" but passes no options** — candidates collapse to `['outputs/concerns.md']`. Behavior is arguably right (rescue machinery canonicalizes at job root; expanding into `<workingDir>/outputs/` would read stale files from the target checkout), so fix the comment rather than the code.

**Finding 4 (SUGESTION?): duplicate read + double surfacing** — skip; intended.

Any other issues? Let me do the final exhaustive re-read of the changed files per the guidelines... Let me re-scan the diff hunks once more:

1. `bug_development.json` / `story_development.json`: +1 line each, correctly placed after output_rules.md. ✅
2. `docs/agents/generated/story_development.md`: generator-clean ✅

4. `instructions/common/completion_post_check.md`: new file. Content check: references "the pipeline appends it to the completion comment and the PR body and labels the ticket `ai_concerns`" — TRUE for 3 of 4 legs (finding 1). Also — the file sits instructions/common/ and is referenced as `instructions/common/completion_post_check.md` — consistent with input_context_reading.md reference style ✅.
5. `js/config.js`: +1 label ✅.
6. `js/developTicketAndCreatePR.js`: reviewed above — findings 2 & 3.
7. `js/unit-tests/test_developTicketAndCreatePR.js`: +210 lines, 11 tests, all passing ✅. Note: `loadForConcernsSeam` — big inline loader, style consistent with the file's existing loaders ✅.
8. snapshots: generator-clean ✅.

🚨 **BLOCKING: the post-check leaks into `bug_fix_batch_development`, but nothing surfaces its concerns there**

`bug_fix_batch_development.json:29` bundles the shared `./agents/instructions/bug_development/general_guidelines.md`, so this line (and the new POSTCHECK flowchart node) land in the **batch leg's prompt** — visible in this PR's own regenerated `snapshots/bug_fix_batch_development.md` hunk. But:

1. **The instruction definition is not bundled** — `completion_post_check.md` is added to `bug_development.json` and `story_development.json` cliPrompts, but not to `bug_fix_batch_development.json`, so the batch agent is told to "run the COMPLETION POST-CHECK — see `instructions/common/completion_post_check.md`" without receiving the file that defines it.
2. **Nothing reads the output** — `js/developBugFixBatchAndCreatePR.js` is a separate implementation (it does not require `developTicketAndCreatePR.js`; grep for `concerns|outputFiles|response.md` finds nothing). It builds its own PR body from epic/bug data and posts its own comment, so an `outputs/concerns.md` written by a batch agent is **never surfaced** — no `ai_concerns` label, no comment section, no PR-body section.

Net effect: on every batch leg with a real integration gap, the agent dutifully writes a concerns file the pipeline silently drops — exactly the failure mode this feature exists to prevent. It is also a scope leak: the PR description only claims the `bug_development`/`story_development` legs.

**Fix (either is acceptable):**
- Wire it: add `./agents/instructions/common/completion_post_check.md` to `bug_fix_batch_development.json` cliPrompts, and have `developBugFixBatchAndCreatePR.js` call the exported `readConcernsMd` / `appendConcernsToCompletionComment` / `mirrorConcernsIntoResponseBody` seams (they are already exported for reuse).
- Or scope it: gate the POSTCHECK node + the "Before finishing" line so the batch flavor of `general_guidelines.md` does not receive them (e.g. move the line into `bug_development/output_rules.md`, which the batch leg does not bundle).

Review complete. All artifacts written and verified; workspace restored to `main` (only the review artifacts in `outputs/` are new).

## PR #1302 Review — `feat(dev): completion post-check` — REQUEST_CHANGES

**What the PR does**: adds a dev-agent "completion post-check" (`outputs/concerns.md` → completion comment + `ai_concerns` label + PR-body mirror), wired into `developTicketAndCreatePR.js`, with 11 new characterization tests.

**Verified green**: full node suite 7764 passed (the single `sessionDelta` failure is pre-existing — fails identically on `main`, sandbox-env artifact); `generate_agent_snapshots.js` and `js/agentDocGenerator.js` both regenerate **byte-identical** to the committed trees; GraalJS constraints respected; exports additive; both Jira/ADO tracker `addLabel(key, label)` signatures match.

**Findings**:
1. 🚨 **BLOCKING** — the shared `instructions/bug_development/general_guidelines.md` change leaks into the `bug_fix_batch_development` leg (bundled at `bug_fix_batch_development.json:29`, visible in the PR's own regenerated `snapshots/bug_fix_batch_development.md` hunk), but that leg neither receives `completion_post_check.md` nor has any surfacing — `developBugFixBatchAndCreatePR.js` is a separate implementation with zero references to `concerns`/`outputFiles`/`response.md`. Batch agents will write a concerns file the pipeline silently drops.
2. ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** — `writeConcernsIntoResponseMd` does `readResponseMd(...) || ''` then unconditionally `file_write`s `outputs/response.md`: a transient re-read failure after the first successful read clobbers the leg's PR-body summary with a concerns-only file (behavior pinned by a test). Guard the blank-base case.
3. 💡 **SUGGESTION** — `readConcernsMd` docstring claims "same candidate expansion as every other output file" but passes no options (job-root read only). The behavior is arguably right (rescue machinery canonicalizes at job root; expansion would risk stale files in the target checkout) — fix the comment, not the code.

Key evidence for the blocking finding (all read this run): `bug_fix_batch_development.json:29` (shared general_guidelines bundled, no completion_post_check.md), `instructions/bug_development/general_guidelines.md:22-25,40` (new POSTCHECK demand), the `snapshots/bug_fix_batch_development.md` hunk in the PR diff (proves the batch prompt receives it), and `js/developBugFixBatchAndCreatePR.js` (own PR-body/comment implementation, no concerns surfacing). Suggested fixes are in `outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md` — wire the seams or scope the shared-instruction change out of the batch flavor.
